excerpts.text: Subsequently, 18 other states adopted term limits, but in four - Massachusetts, Oregon, Washington and Wyoming- term limits were thrown out by the state supreme courts, and they have been repealed by the legislatures in Idaho and Utah. That leaves 15 states with term limits for legislators.
Term limits have been changed occasionally; most recently, Arkansas extended its term limits from six years in the House and eight years in the Senate to a 16 year cumulative total.

The tempo increased dramatically in 1998 when time ran out for another 204 members in both chambers in California, Colorado and Maine, the Missouri Senate, and the Arkansas, Michigan and Oregon House chambers.

excerpts.text:
Text of Article 1, Section 2:

The House of Representatives shall be composed of Members chosen every second Year by the People of the several States, and the Electors in each State shall have the Qualifications requisite for Electors of the most numerous Branch of the State Legislature.

assessment.provenance_note: Additional qualification clause for Representatives (age 25, 7 years citizenship, state inhabitant) provided but does not address term length.
assessment.rationale: Span 124 lists qualification requirements but does not mention term length; provides contextual qualifications only.
limitations: Term length not addressed in this span

excerpts.text: No Person shall be a Representative who shall not have attained to the Age of twenty five Years, and been seven Years a Citizen of the United States, and who shall not, when elected, be an Inhabitant of that State in which he shall be chosen.

assessment.provenance_note: Spans 7 and 13 describe Senate six-year terms; span 13 explicitly corrects that House terms are two years, not six.
assessment.rationale: The assertion that 'The United States Constitution sets a six-year term for members of the House of Representatives' is contradicted by span 13, which states the Framers reduced a proposed seven-year Senate term to six years, while the House term is two years (implied by span 19). limitations: Spans do not explicitly enumerate the House term length in a single sentence, requiring inference from context.

flags.explanation: The source addresses Senate terms (six years) but does not set the House term; the claim incorrectly assigns six-year terms to the House.

excerpts.text: The Senate of the United States shall be composed of two Senators from each State, chosen by the Legislature thereof, for six Years; and each Senator shall have one Vote.

Max Farrand, The Framing of the Constitution 76 (1913). the Framers reduced the seven-year Senate term, which had been discussed in conjunction with the three-year House term, to six years. *Id.* at 91.

limitations: Does not quote constitutional text establishing the House term.

excerpts.text: Commentators have viewed the six-year Senate term and two-year House term as striking a careful balance between institutional stability provided by a longer Senate term and legislative responsiveness provided by shorter House terms punctuated by frequent elections.
